--- title: 03 · Trade communities (Louvain) --- **RQ2 — do trade communities emerge, and do they follow geography?** Runs weighted Louvain on the undirected projection of both the full graph and the backbone, keeps whichever partition is clearer, and maps the result. The projection and the modularity criterion are described on the [Data & method](../data.qmd) page. The partition found here is also browsable as an [interactive network](../network.qmd). ::: {#1 .cell quarto-private-1='{"key":"execution","value":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-27T06:39:21.678006Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-27T06:39:21.677935Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-27T06:39:21.913751Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-27T06:39:21.913076Z"}}' execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from __future__ import annotations import pandas as pd from IPython.display import Markdown, display from eu_trade_network import communities, config, data_loader, db, graph, metrics, viz ``` ::: ## Graph + undirected projections Rebuild the edge list / digraph for `config.YEAR`, compute centralities (for node strengths), and build the undirected-weighted projection plus its backbone counterpart. ::: {#3 .cell quarto-private-1='{"key":"execution","value":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-27T06:39:21.914808Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-27T06:39:21.914668Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.357610Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.357067Z"}}' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} edgelist = data_loader.build_edgelist() G = graph.build_graph(edgelist) cent = metrics.compute_centralities(G) node_meta = ( pd.DataFrame([{"iso3": n, **attrs} for n, attrs in G.nodes(data=True)]) .sort_values("iso3") .reset_index(drop=True) ) nodes_db = node_meta.merge(cent, on="iso3", how="inner") und_full = communities.to_undirected_weighted(G) backbone = metrics.disparity_filter(G, alpha=config.DISPARITY_ALPHA) und_bb = communities.to_undirected_weighted(backbone) print( f"Full projection: {und_full.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {und_full.number_of_edges()} edges; " f"backbone projection: {und_bb.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {und_bb.number_of_edges()} edges" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Full projection: 35 nodes, 595 edges; backbone projection: 35 nodes, 122 edges ``` ::: ::: ## Detect communities — full graph vs backbone Run weighted Louvain on both projections and keep the clearer result (higher modularity). ::: {#5 .cell quarto-private-1='{"key":"execution","value":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.358606Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.358494Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.364648Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.364153Z"}}' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} part_full = communities.detect_communities(und_full) mod_full = communities.modularity(und_full, part_full) part_bb = communities.detect_communities(und_bb) mod_bb = communities.modularity(und_bb, part_bb) # Keep the clearer partition: higher modularity = better-separated blocs. if mod_bb >= mod_full: chosen_name, undirected, partition, chosen_mod = "backbone", und_bb, part_bb, mod_bb else: chosen_name, undirected, partition, chosen_mod = "full graph", und_full, part_full, mod_full print(f"Full graph: {len(set(part_full.values()))} communities, Q = {mod_full:.4f}") print(f"Backbone: {len(set(part_bb.values()))} communities, Q = {mod_bb:.4f}") print( f"→ Keeping the {chosen_name} partition " f"({len(set(partition.values()))} communities, Q = {chosen_mod:.4f})." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Full graph: 3 communities, Q = 0.1509 Backbone: 3 communities, Q = 0.2515 → Keeping the backbone partition (3 communities, Q = 0.2515). ``` ::: ::: ## Persist community ids in DuckDB Write the chosen community assignment (plus refreshed centralities) into the `nodes` table. ::: {#7 .cell quarto-private-1='{"key":"execution","value":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.365441Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.365371Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.412698Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.412143Z"}}' execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} nodes_db["community"] = [int(partition[i]) for i in nodes_db["iso3"]] con = db.connect() db.init_schema(con) db.write_table( con, "nodes", nodes_db[ [ "iso3", "name", "grp", "out_strength", "in_strength", "degree", "betweenness", "betweenness_u", "eigenvector", "pagerank", "community", ] ], ) # Keep edges in sync if earlier notebooks have not been run in this environment. edges_db = edgelist.copy() edges_db["year"] = config.YEAR db.write_table(con, "edges", edges_db[["exporter_iso3", "importer_iso3", "value_kusd", "year"]]) print(f"Wrote community ids for {len(nodes_db)} nodes → {config.DB_PATH}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Wrote community ids for 35 nodes → /home/emilia/portfolio/eu-trade-network/data/processed/trade.duckdb ``` ::: ::: ## Community summary (RQ2) Size, members, and total exports per community, straight from SQL. ::: {#9 .cell quarto-private-1='{"key":"execution","value":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.413609Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.413535Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.433952Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.433441Z"}}' execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} community_tbl = db.read_sql(con, config.SQL_DIR / "queries" / "02_community_summary.sql") community_tbl ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
community n_countries members community_exports_busd
0 0 23 DEU, NLD, ITA, FRA, BEL, ESP, POL, CHE, CZE, A... 5237.2
1 1 7 CHN, USA, JPN, RUS, GBR, IRL, TUR 3894.2
2 2 5 NOR, SWE, DNK, FIN, EST 623.5
``` ::: ::: ## Geographic map coloured by community Nodes at lon/lat, coloured by Louvain community and sized by export strength; faint lines show the backbone so the blocs are readable against geography. ::: {#11 .cell quarto-private-1='{"key":"execution","value":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.434770Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-27T06:39:26.434698Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.025992Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.025348Z"}}' execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} bb_edges = pd.DataFrame( [ {"exporter_iso3": u, "importer_iso3": v, "value_kusd": float(d["weight"])} for u, v, d in backbone.edges(data=True) ] ) fig_comm = viz.plot_community_map( nodes_db, partition, edgelist=bb_edges, title=( f"European trade communities — Louvain on the {chosen_name} " f"(K={len(set(partition.values()))}, Q={chosen_mod:.3f})" ), ) out = viz.save_fig(fig_comm, "03_community_map.png", headline=True) print(f"Saved {out}") fig_comm.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Saved /home/emilia/portfolio/eu-trade-network/figures/headline/03_community_map.png ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interactive network Write the PyVis HTML used by the site's [interactive network](../network.qmd) page (node size ∝ strength, colour = community, edge width ∝ bilateral value). Explore it there rather than here. ::: {#13 .cell quarto-private-1='{"key":"execution","value":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.026952Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.026859Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.085743Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.085234Z"}}' execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Short, data-driven legend labels: name each bloc after its largest exporter. strength_by_iso = dict(zip(nodes_db["iso3"], nodes_db["out_strength"], strict=True)) members_by_comm: dict[int, list[str]] = {} for iso, comm in partition.items(): members_by_comm.setdefault(int(comm), []).append(iso) community_labels = { comm: ( f"{max(members, key=lambda i: strength_by_iso.get(i, 0.0))}-led bloc " f"({len(members)} economies)" ) for comm, members in members_by_comm.items() } k = len(set(partition.values())) html_path = config.PROJECT_ROOT / "network_viz" / "03_trade_communities.html" viz.plot_network_pyvis( undirected, partition, html_path, title="European trade communities", subtitle=f"Weighted Louvain on the {chosen_name} · K={k} · modularity Q={chosen_mod:.3f}", community_labels=community_labels, ) print(f"Wrote interactive network → {html_path}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Wrote interactive network → /home/emilia/portfolio/eu-trade-network/network_viz/03_trade_communities.html ``` ::: ::: ## Do the blocs follow EU membership or geography? The paragraph below is generated from the chosen partition, so it always matches the run. ::: {#15 .cell quarto-private-1='{"key":"execution","value":{"iopub.execute_input":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.086656Z","iopub.status.busy":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.086507Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.127568Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-07-27T06:39:28.126948Z"}}' execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} summary_tbl = communities.community_summary(partition, nodes_db, undirected=undirected) eu_set = set(config.EU27) blocs = [] for _, row in summary_tbl.iterrows(): members = row["members"].split(", ") n_eu = sum(m in eu_set for m in members) blocs.append( f"- **Community {int(row['community'])}** — {int(row['n_countries'])} economies, " f"{n_eu} of them EU-27: {row['members']}" ) eu_communities = {partition[c] for c in config.EU27 if c in partition} verdict = ( f"**Modularity Q = {chosen_mod:.3f}** on the {chosen_name} — moderate but real community " "structure for a densely integrated trade network. The EU-27 does **not** form a single " f"bloc: it splits across **{len(eu_communities)} communities**. Membership shows through " "regionally — a large German-anchored continental core plus a Nordic-Baltic cluster — but " "the partition tracks *geography and trade intensity*, not the EU border: non-members " "Switzerland and Norway sit inside their neighbouring EU clusters, while EU-member Ireland " "defects to the extra-European bloc built around the US, China and the UK (its trade is " "dominated by US-linked pharma/tech). **Blocs are geographic, not political.**" ) display(Markdown("\n".join(blocs) + "\n\n" + verdict)) con.close() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} - **Community 0** — 23 economies, 22 of them EU-27: DEU, NLD, ITA, FRA, BEL, ESP, POL, CHE, CZE, AUT, HUN, SVK, ROU, PRT, SVN, BGR, LTU, GRC, HRV, LVA, LUX, MLT, CYP - **Community 1** — 7 economies, 1 of them EU-27: CHN, USA, JPN, RUS, GBR, IRL, TUR - **Community 2** — 5 economies, 4 of them EU-27: NOR, SWE, DNK, FIN, EST **Modularity Q = 0.251** on the backbone — moderate but real community structure for a densely integrated trade network. The EU-27 does **not** form a single bloc: it splits across **3 communities**. Membership shows through regionally — a large German-anchored continental core plus a Nordic-Baltic cluster — but the partition tracks *geography and trade intensity*, not the EU border: non-members Switzerland and Norway sit inside their neighbouring EU clusters, while EU-member Ireland defects to the extra-European bloc built around the US, China and the UK (its trade is dominated by US-linked pharma/tech). **Blocs are geographic, not political.** ::: :::
